name: AI Security Institute
mandate: Evaluates frontier AI models for security risks; research organisation within the Cabinet Office. The UK coordinates the international network.
mandate_short: Tests frontier AI models for security and safety risks.
reports_to_notes: A written answer of 18 November 2026 says the institute is led by two Directors, who report to the Director General for Artificial Intelligence and Head of the Prime Minister's AI Taskforce, within the Office for the Prime Minister and Cabinet; it names neither Director.

testing_capacity_notes: Further own testing: joint pre-deployment evaluations with the US institute of the upgraded Claude 3.5 Sonnet (November 2024) and OpenAI o1 (December 2024), a joint assessment of Kimi K3 with the US institute (July 2026) and its own evaluation of GPT-6 Astra (September 2026). model_access_notes: Event dates are the model's public release date in Epoch AI's data unless the source dates the access itself; for every event except Gemini 4 Argon the sources state that the access came before release, so the access took place on or before that date. The Epoch AI models cited for the leading-developer test were released at least a month before each such date. Not counted: Kimi K3 (Moonshot, July 2026), as the access route is not stated; the Llama 3.1-405B network pilot (October to November 2024), as its weights are public. The developer agreements are the commitments of Anthropic, Google DeepMind and OpenAI to give the institute's predecessor 'deep model access', announced in 2023. The institute says it has independently evaluated more than 55 models before release, working with industry; the post names no models, so they are not counted as access events. Gemini 4 Argon is dated 13 October 2026, Epoch AI's release date; Google announced it on 30 September 2026, when it was rolling out to a set of trusted cyber defenders through Google's Fairwind Program, with an initial cohort of cyber defenders and trusted testers, and release to developers, enterprises and consumers, starting with paid API customers and Google AI Ultra subscribers, was to follow. The sources do not date the institute's access. A written answer of 2 November 2026 says all the institute's current collaboration agreements are with developers based in the UK and the US; one of 6 November says its evaluations are governed by agreements with the developers and their results are not typically published. A House of Commons committee report of 18 November 2026 says the institute has no guaranteed statutory right of access to models and that access before release is voluntary; it recommends a statutory AI regulator separate from the institute. The institute's Director wrote to a House of Commons committee on 15 September 2026 that Anthropic had made clear, when it released Mythos 5.1, that no organisation outside the US had access to the model. Anthropic's letter of 22 October 2026 to a House of Commons committee says that, while the US government considered a new framework for pre-deployment testing and access, it could not give the institute access to Mythos 5.1 without safeguards before deployment and offered access with safeguards; it says it has since been able to give the institute access without safeguards to its latest models before deployment. Anthropic's witness told the committee on 13 October 2026 that the institute decided not to use the restricted access and has access to the model now.

testing_capacity_source_ids: de-breg; de-bmds; de-bsi-aisi; de-uk-statement-full-2026; de-bt-8727-2026; de-ki-taskforce-2030
testing_capacity_notes: Focus statement, not counted as testing: in the first phase of operation 'liegt ein wichtiger Schwerpunkt in der Analyse und Bewertung führender KI-Modelle' (an important focus is the analysis and assessment of leading AI models). In a first phase the Federal Office for Information Security (BSI) and the Federal Network Agency form a virtual nucleus of the institute. BSI's institute page says 'Zurzeit befindet sich das Institut noch im Aufbau. Der Fokus liegt zunächst auf der Beratung von Verwaltung und Politik' (the institute is still being set up; the initial focus is advising government and policy-makers). The government's answer of 19 October 2026 says the institute initially pools existing BSI and BNetzA capabilities and uses and develops existing testing and evaluation methods. It says no separate posts are allocated for the first phase, and that technical equipment and further capacity remain under discussion. The UK-Germany joint statement of 30 June 2026 says both countries 'will share best practice on AI evaluation'. The federal government's AI taskforce report 'Deutschland als KI-Nation 2030' of 2 November 2026 sets a target for 2030 that the institute examine and assess at least 75 per cent of new frontier AI models for security-policy impact within four months.
model_access_notes: BSI states 'Das AISI Deutschland übernimmt ausdrücklich keine Regulierungs- oder Marktüberwachungsfunktion' (AISI Deutschland expressly takes on no regulatory or market-surveillance function). The government's written answer of 6 October 2026 to a parliamentary question says the institute has 'eine wichtige Rolle beim Zugang zu Frontier-KI-Modellen, der internationalen Vernetzung und bei der Bewertung von Sicherheitsrisiken und -anforderungen' (an important role in access to frontier AI models, international networking and assessing security risks and requirements).
